work.title: The First Part of Henry the Sixth
work.author: William Shakespeare

scene.label: Act 2, Scene 4
scene.title: SCENE IV. London. The Temple Garden.

content.text: Enter the Earls of Somerset, Suffolk, and Warwick; Richard Plantagenet, Vernon and another Lawyer.

lines.text: Great lords and gentlemen, what means this silence?
lines.plainText: Great lords and gentlemen what means this silence

lines.text: Dare no man answer in a case of truth?
lines.plainText: Dare no man answer in a case of truth

lines.text: Within the Temple Hall we were too loud;
lines.plainText: Within the Temple Hall we were too loud

lines.text: The garden here is more convenient.
lines.plainText: The garden here is more convenient

lines.text: Then say at once if I maintain'd the truth;
lines.plainText: Then say at once if I maintain'd the truth

lines.text: Or else was wrangling Somerset in th' error?
lines.plainText: Or else was wrangling Somerset in th' error

lines.text: Faith, I have been a truant in the law
lines.plainText: Faith I have been a truant in the law

lines.text: And never yet could frame my will to it;
lines.plainText: And never yet could frame my will to it

lines.text: And therefore frame the law unto my will.
lines.plainText: And therefore frame the law unto my will

lines.text: Judge you, my Lord of Warwick, then, between us.
lines.plainText: Judge you my Lord of Warwick then between us

lines.text: Between two hawks, which flies the higher pitch;
lines.plainText: Between two hawks which flies the higher pitch

lines.text: Between two dogs, which hath the deeper mouth;
lines.plainText: Between two dogs which hath the deeper mouth

lines.text: Between two blades, which bears the better temper;
lines.plainText: Between two blades which bears the better temper

lines.text: Between two horses, which doth bear him best;
lines.plainText: Between two horses which doth bear him best

lines.text: Between two girls, which hath the merriest eye;
lines.plainText: Between two girls which hath the merriest eye

lines.text: I have perhaps some shallow spirit of judgement;
lines.plainText: I have perhaps some shallow spirit of judgement

lines.text: But in these nice sharp quillets of the law,
lines.plainText: But in these nice sharp quillets of the law

lines.text: Good faith, I am no wiser than a daw.
lines.plainText: Good faith I am no wiser than a daw

lines.text: Tut, tut, here is a mannerly forbearance!
lines.plainText: Tut tut here is a mannerly forbearance

lines.text: The truth appears so naked on my side
lines.plainText: The truth appears so naked on my side

lines.text: That any purblind eye may find it out.
lines.plainText: That any purblind eye may find it out

lines.text: And on my side it is so well apparell'd,
lines.plainText: And on my side it is so well apparell'd

lines.text: So clear, so shining and so evident,
lines.plainText: So clear so shining and so evident

lines.text: That it will glimmer through a blind man's eye.
lines.plainText: That it will glimmer through a blind man's eye

lines.text: Since you are tongue-tied and so loath to speak,
lines.plainText: Since you are tonguetied and so loath to speak

lines.text: In dumb significants proclaim your thoughts:
lines.plainText: In dumb significants proclaim your thoughts

lines.text: Let him that is a true-born gentleman
lines.plainText: Let him that is a trueborn gentleman

lines.text: And stands upon the honour of his birth,
lines.plainText: And stands upon the honour of his birth

lines.text: If he suppose that I have pleaded truth,
lines.plainText: If he suppose that I have pleaded truth

lines.text: From off this brier pluck a white rose with me.
lines.plainText: From off this brier pluck a white rose with me

lines.text: Let him that is no coward nor no flatterer,
lines.plainText: Let him that is no coward nor no flatterer

lines.text: But dare maintain the party of the truth,
lines.plainText: But dare maintain the party of the truth

lines.text: Pluck a red rose from off this thorn with me.
lines.plainText: Pluck a red rose from off this thorn with me

lines.text: I love no colours, and without all colour
lines.plainText: I love no colours and without all colour

lines.text: Of base insinuating flattery
lines.plainText: Of base insinuating flattery

lines.text: I pluck this white rose with Plantagenet.
lines.plainText: I pluck this white rose with Plantagenet

lines.text: I pluck this red rose with young Somerset,
lines.plainText: I pluck this red rose with young Somerset

lines.text: And say withal I think he held the right.
lines.plainText: And say withal I think he held the right

lines.text: Stay, lords and gentlemen, and pluck no more
lines.plainText: Stay lords and gentlemen and pluck no more

lines.text: Till you conclude that he upon whose side
lines.plainText: Till you conclude that he upon whose side

lines.text: The fewest roses are cropp'd from the tree
lines.plainText: The fewest roses are cropp'd from the tree

lines.text: Shall yield the other in the right opinion.
lines.plainText: Shall yield the other in the right opinion

lines.text: Good Master Vernon, it is well objected:
lines.plainText: Good Master Vernon it is well objected

lines.text: If I have fewest, I subscribe in silence.
lines.plainText: If I have fewest I subscribe in silence

lines.text: And I.
lines.plainText: And I

lines.text: Then for the truth and plainness of the case,
lines.plainText: Then for the truth and plainness of the case

lines.text: I pluck this pale and maiden blossom here,
lines.plainText: I pluck this pale and maiden blossom here

lines.text: Giving my verdict on the white rose side.
lines.plainText: Giving my verdict on the white rose side

lines.text: Prick not your finger as you pluck it off,
lines.plainText: Prick not your finger as you pluck it off

lines.text: Lest, bleeding, you do paint the white rose red,
lines.plainText: Lest bleeding you do paint the white rose red

lines.text: And fall on my side so against your will.
lines.plainText: And fall on my side so against your will

lines.text: If I, my lord, for my opinion bleed,
lines.plainText: If I my lord for my opinion bleed

lines.text: Opinion shall be surgeon to my hurt
lines.plainText: Opinion shall be surgeon to my hurt

lines.text: And keep me on the side where still I am.
lines.plainText: And keep me on the side where still I am

lines.text: Well, well, come on, who else?
lines.plainText: Well well come on who else

lines.text: Unless my study and my books be false,
lines.plainText: Unless my study and my books be false

lines.text: Now, Somerset, where is your argument?
lines.plainText: Now Somerset where is your argument

lines.text: Here in my scabbard, meditating that
lines.plainText: Here in my scabbard meditating that

lines.text: Shall dye your white rose in a bloody red.
lines.plainText: Shall dye your white rose in a bloody red

lines.text: Meantime your cheeks do counterfeit our roses;
lines.plainText: Meantime your cheeks do counterfeit our roses

lines.text: For pale they look with fear, as witnessing
lines.plainText: For pale they look with fear as witnessing

lines.text: The truth on our side.
lines.plainText: The truth on our side

lines.text: No, Plantagenet,
lines.plainText: No Plantagenet

lines.text: 'Tis not for fear but anger that thy cheeks
lines.plainText: 'Tis not for fear but anger that thy cheeks

lines.text: Blush for pure shame to counterfeit our roses,
lines.plainText: Blush for pure shame to counterfeit our roses

lines.text: And yet thy tongue will not confess thy error.
lines.plainText: And yet thy tongue will not confess thy error

lines.text: Hath not thy rose a canker, Somerset?
lines.plainText: Hath not thy rose a canker Somerset

lines.text: Hath not thy rose a thorn, Plantagenet?
lines.plainText: Hath not thy rose a thorn Plantagenet

lines.text: Ay, sharp and piercing, to maintain his truth;
lines.plainText: Ay sharp and piercing to maintain his truth

lines.text: Whiles thy consuming canker eats his falsehood.
lines.plainText: Whiles thy consuming canker eats his falsehood

lines.text: Well, I'll find friends to wear my bleeding roses,
lines.plainText: Well I'll find friends to wear my bleeding roses

lines.text: That shall maintain what I have said is true,
lines.plainText: That shall maintain what I have said is true

lines.text: Where false Plantagenet dare not be seen.
lines.plainText: Where false Plantagenet dare not be seen

lines.text: Now, by this maiden blossom in my hand,
lines.plainText: Now by this maiden blossom in my hand

lines.text: I scorn thee and thy fashion, peevish boy.
lines.plainText: I scorn thee and thy fashion peevish boy

lines.text: Turn not thy scorns this way, Plantagenet.
lines.plainText: Turn not thy scorns this way Plantagenet

lines.text: Proud Pole, I will, and scorn both him and thee.
lines.plainText: Proud Pole I will and scorn both him and thee

lines.text: I'll turn my part thereof into thy throat.
lines.plainText: I'll turn my part thereof into thy throat

lines.text: Away, away, good William de la Pole!
lines.plainText: Away away good William de la Pole

lines.text: We grace the yeoman by conversing with him.
lines.plainText: We grace the yeoman by conversing with him

lines.text: Now, by God's will, thou wrong'st him, Somerset;
lines.plainText: Now by God's will thou wrong'st him Somerset

lines.text: His grandfather was Lionel Duke of Clarence,
lines.plainText: His grandfather was Lionel Duke of Clarence

lines.text: Third son to the third Edward King of England.
lines.plainText: Third son to the third Edward King of England

lines.text: Spring crestless yeomen from so deep a root?
lines.plainText: Spring crestless yeomen from so deep a root

lines.text: He bears him on the place's privilege,
lines.plainText: He bears him on the place's privilege

lines.text: Or durst not for his craven heart, say thus.
lines.plainText: Or durst not for his craven heart say thus

lines.text: By Him that made me, I'll maintain my words
lines.plainText: By Him that made me I'll maintain my words

lines.text: On any plot of ground in Christendom.
lines.plainText: On any plot of ground in Christendom

lines.text: Was not thy father, Richard Earl of Cambridge,
lines.plainText: Was not thy father Richard Earl of Cambridge

lines.text: For treason executed in our late king's days?
lines.plainText: For treason executed in our late king's days

lines.text: And, by his treason, stand'st not thou attainted,
lines.plainText: And by his treason stand'st not thou attainted

lines.text: Corrupted, and exempt from ancient gentry?
lines.plainText: Corrupted and exempt from ancient gentry

lines.text: His trespass yet lives guilty in thy blood;
lines.plainText: His trespass yet lives guilty in thy blood

lines.text: And, till thou be restored, thou art a yeoman.
lines.plainText: And till thou be restored thou art a yeoman

lines.text: My father was attached, not attainted,
lines.plainText: My father was attached not attainted

lines.text: Condemn'd to die for treason, but no traitor;
lines.plainText: Condemn'd to die for treason but no traitor

lines.text: And that I'll prove on better men than Somerset,
lines.plainText: And that I'll prove on better men than Somerset

lines.text: Were growing time once ripen'd to my will.
lines.plainText: Were growing time once ripen'd to my will

lines.text: For your partaker Pole and you yourself,
lines.plainText: For your partaker Pole and you yourself

lines.text: I'll note you in my book of memory,
lines.plainText: I'll note you in my book of memory

lines.text: To scourge you for this apprehension.
lines.plainText: To scourge you for this apprehension

lines.text: Look to it well, and say you are well warn'd.
lines.plainText: Look to it well and say you are well warn'd

lines.text: Ah, thou shalt find us ready for thee still;
lines.plainText: Ah thou shalt find us ready for thee still

lines.text: And know us by these colours for thy foes,
lines.plainText: And know us by these colours for thy foes

lines.text: For these my friends in spite of thee shall wear.
lines.plainText: For these my friends in spite of thee shall wear

lines.text: And, by my soul, this pale and angry rose,
lines.plainText: And by my soul this pale and angry rose

lines.text: As cognizance of my blood-drinking hate,
lines.plainText: As cognizance of my blooddrinking hate

lines.text: Will I for ever and my faction wear,
lines.plainText: Will I for ever and my faction wear

lines.text: Until it wither with me to my grave,
lines.plainText: Until it wither with me to my grave

lines.text: Or flourish to the height of my degree.
lines.plainText: Or flourish to the height of my degree

lines.text: Go forward, and be chok'd with thy ambition!
lines.plainText: Go forward and be chok'd with thy ambition

lines.text: And so farewell until I meet thee next.
lines.plainText: And so farewell until I meet thee next

lines.text: Have with thee, Pole. Farewell, ambitious Richard.
lines.plainText: Have with thee Pole Farewell ambitious Richard

lines.text: How I am braved and must perforce endure it!
lines.plainText: How I am braved and must perforce endure it

lines.text: This blot that they object against your house
lines.plainText: This blot that they object against your house

lines.text: Shall be wiped out in the next parliament
lines.plainText: Shall be wiped out in the next parliament

lines.text: Call'd for the truce of Winchester and Gloucester;
lines.plainText: Call'd for the truce of Winchester and Gloucester

lines.text: And if thou be not then created York,
lines.plainText: And if thou be not then created York

lines.text: I will not live to be accounted Warwick.
lines.plainText: I will not live to be accounted Warwick

lines.text: Meantime, in signal of my love to thee,
lines.plainText: Meantime in signal of my love to thee

lines.text: Against proud Somerset and William Pole,
lines.plainText: Against proud Somerset and William Pole

lines.text: Will I upon thy party wear this rose.
lines.plainText: Will I upon thy party wear this rose

lines.text: And here I prophesy: this brawl today,
lines.plainText: And here I prophesy this brawl today

lines.text: Grown to this faction in the Temple Garden,
lines.plainText: Grown to this faction in the Temple Garden

lines.text: Shall send between the Red Rose and the White
lines.plainText: Shall send between the Red Rose and the White

lines.text: A thousand souls to death and deadly night.
lines.plainText: A thousand souls to death and deadly night

lines.text: Good Master Vernon, I am bound to you,
lines.plainText: Good Master Vernon I am bound to you

lines.text: That you on my behalf would pluck a flower.
lines.plainText: That you on my behalf would pluck a flower

lines.text: In your behalf still will I wear the same.
lines.plainText: In your behalf still will I wear the same

lines.text: And so will I.
lines.plainText: And so will I

lines.text: Thanks, gentlemen.
lines.plainText: Thanks gentlemen

lines.text: Come, let us four to dinner. I dare say
lines.plainText: Come let us four to dinner I dare say

lines.text: This quarrel will drink blood another day.
lines.plainText: This quarrel will drink blood another day
